name: IRELAND
lead: Ireland is a small island at the western edge of Europe, wrapped in forty shades of green. Atlantic rain keeps everything lush. It has ancient castles and lively music in cosy pubs. More Irish people live abroad than on the island.
geo: Green fields are divided by stone walls, dotted with glassy lakes called loughs. Rain falls about 150 days a year, keeping everything green.
The Cliffs of Moher rise 214 m from the Atlantic. In the Burren, a high, flat area of limestone rock, Arctic, Alpine and Mediterranean wildflowers grow side by side.
animals: The red deer, Ireland's largest land mammal, roams Killarney National Park. Grey seals bob in cold bays.
The Irish hare is a chunkier cousin of the brown hare. White-tailed eagles vanished for a century. They were brought back in 2007.
culture: The harp is Ireland's national emblem, the only musical instrument that is any country's emblem. Traditional sessions (seisiún) fill pubs with fiddles, flutes and bodhrán drums.
Storytelling is a national art. Ireland has four Nobel Prize-winning writers. Halloween began here as Samhain, an ancient Celtic festival.
history: Irish monks kept learning alive through Europe's Dark Ages by copying books by hand. Vikings raided in the 800s, then settled. They founded Dublin around the year 841.
The 1916 Easter Rising, a rebellion, sparked a war for independence from Britain. The Irish Free State began in 1922. The Republic was proclaimed in 1949.
wows: The monks' Book of Kells, from around the year 800, is so detailed they may have used a lens.
Glaciers and sea, not St Patrick, keep Ireland snake-free.
The Guinness brewery signed a 9,000-year lease (rental deal) on its Dublin site in 1759.
Newgrange tomb (3,200 BCE) is hundreds of years older than Stonehenge and the pyramids.
Ireland exports more software than any other European country.
Ogham, an old alphabet carved on standing stones, is over 1,500 years old.
On the year's shortest day, sunrise shines down Newgrange's passage, built 5,000 years ago.

myths.myth: Ireland is always cold and grey
myths.fact: The Gulf Stream, a warm sea current, keeps Ireland mild. Dublin rarely sees snow. Daffodils often bloom in February.

myths.myth: St Patrick was born in Ireland
myths.fact: Patrick was born in Roman Britain. Raiders took him to Ireland as a teenage slave.
